title: Why did my transaction fail? Common errors in plain English
seoTitle: Why Did My Transaction Fail? Common Errors Explained | CRYPY
description: Out of gas, slippage, insufficient allowance, expired deadline: what common blockchain transaction errors mean, why you still paid a fee, and what helps.
summary: Out of gas, slippage, insufficient allowance and more: what each error means and what helps.
inShort: A failed transaction is undone, but you still pay for the gas it used.
Most failures come from a few causes: gas, slippage, allowance, balance or deadlines.
The contract's error message usually says which one.

sections.heading: Why you paid a fee for nothing

blocks.text: When a transaction fails inside a block, every change it tried to make is undone: no tokens move. But validators still did the work of running it up to the point it failed, so the network fee for the gas it used is kept.
A transaction that never made it into a block (for example one rejected by your wallet or replaced) costs nothing.

sections.heading: Common errors and what they mean

items: **Out of gas:** the gas limit was too low for what the transaction had to do. It usually used nearly all of its gas limit. Try again with the wallet's suggested limit.
**Insufficient funds for gas:** you don't have enough ETH, BNB or POL to pay the fee, even if you hold tokens. Keep a little of the chain's coin for fees.

**Slippage ("too little received", "INSUFFICIENT_OUTPUT_AMOUNT"):** the price moved between sending and execution by more than your tolerance. Try again, or raise slippage a little for volatile tokens.
**Deadline expired ("EXPIRED", "Transaction too old"):** a swap waited too long before being included. Try again, maybe with a higher priority fee.
**Insufficient allowance ("transfer amount exceeds allowance"):** the app wasn't approved to spend that much of your token. Approve first, then retry.
**Insufficient balance ("transfer amount exceeds balance"):** you tried to send or swap more than you hold.
**Transfer failed ("TRANSFER_FAILED"):** often a token that blocks or taxes transfers. If it happens when selling, check the token: see [What is a honeypot token](guide:honeypot-token).
**Paused or not allowed:** the contract is paused, or your address isn't permitted to do that.

blocks.text: Transactions from one wallet go in order, numbered by a **nonce**. If an earlier transaction is waiting with a low fee, later ones wait behind it. Most wallets let you speed it up or cancel it by sending a replacement with the same nonce and a higher fee.

Paste the transaction hash into the [Transaction Checker](tool:tx-checker). It shows the result, the contract's own error message when the node still has the data to read it, a plain-English explanation of well-known errors, and how much gas was used.

items: Keep some of the chain's coin for fees.
Use the gas limit your wallet suggests.
For volatile tokens, a slightly higher slippage tolerance avoids failures; very high slippage invites bad prices.
If a wallet warns that a transaction is likely to fail, don't send it.

faq.q: Can I get the fee back for a failed transaction?
faq.a: No. The fee pays for the work the network did, even though the result was undone.

faq.q: My tokens left my wallet but the transaction failed. Where are they?
faq.a: If the transaction failed, nothing moved. Check your balance again, and check the transaction on the Transaction Checker to be sure which one you are looking at.

faq.q: Why does the error message say nothing useful?
faq.a: Some contracts fail without a message, and some nodes can't replay older transactions. The Transaction Checker says when the reason isn't available instead of guessing.
